items.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had Cozy Cole’s Crescendo in Drums. I liked that.

ctx.x: I had very good ears. I could hear like a monster. Jo Jones. Jonathan “Jo” Jones. That was the guy that I – I dug that sound or feeling he got. Chick Webb – I had the record Liza by Chick Webb. I was a youngster when I bought that. I had Cozy Cole’s Crescendo in Drums. I liked that. I could hear just a couple of beats by different drummers that really intrigued me: Shadow Wilson, Queer Street, with Basie. I think he had a four-bar break in there. I had met him anyhow. I met Shadow. I met Kenny Clarke, early,…
Where were they playing, and how did you get a chance to meet these gentlemen?

items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...try to play like Max or Roy Haynes or Elvin or Buddy...

ctx.x: They get a few cliches under their fingers, but they really don't know what he's doing... or for that matter sax players who try to play like Coltrane.

Impossible, see 'cause Coltrane came up in that school, you know, good foundation, working with those bands, different bands, different style bands, and they try to pick up right where Coltrane is now before he died, or the same way with the drummers, try to play like Max or Roy Haynes or Elvin or Buddy, and you just can't you know, it's impossible to be made a doctor over night. There's no way in the world that I've said it over and over, that you can skip grade school and go to high school. See, you've got to…
Do the students that you go to Capital with, is this basically what you tell them?
